To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the cognitive load of an educational activity can be reduced by presenting the content in a way that minimizes the need to process information that is irrelevant to the goal of learning, and (b) cognitive load is a key factor that affects learning.

(1) the cognitive load theory (CL) effects of worked examples are not limited to the initial learning phase but can be found in transfer situations, and (2) the CL effects of worked examples depend on the type of worked example and the type of transfer task.
Cognitive load theory (Sweller, 1988, 1989, 1999, 2003, 2004, 2005) is the most important and influential theory in educational psychology in the last 25 years.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the processes that occur during learning and the conditions that influence those processes (Sweller 2003).
the cognitive processes that occur when people learn and the factors that affect these processes.
the design of effective learning environments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CLT does not meet the rigor of a scientific theory, but it has provided valuable insights for instructional design and has stimulated a number of studies on cognitive processing.
CLT is not a scientific theory in the sense that the term is understood by the scientific community (Kuhn 1970).
the theory of cognitive load has not yet been proven to be a scientific theory.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the theory of cognitive load is a theory that has been proven to work. It is not a theory that can be proven to work.
CLT is not a theory, but rather a set of hypotheses that have been tested and found to have some explanatory power in a number of contexts.
the theory has been successful in inspiring a large body of research, but that the theory is not sufficiently rigorous to be considered as a scientific theory in the truest sense of the word.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the CLT’s scientific rigor needs to be strengthened by a more systematic integration of the cognitive and the affective aspects of learning and by a stronger focus on the learning process and its outcomes.

the CLT’s conceptualization of the learner as a cognitive machine that can be manipulated by instructional designers and its focus on cognitive processes and outcomes have led to an impoverished view of learning and to a narrow focus on instructional design.
the scientific value of CLT can be strengthened by adopting a more comprehensive approach to cognitive load and by integrating CLT with the broader science of learning.
